Flag Atlas / Predictions & corrections / enable_ufc_for_speed
Gboard developer flag · Predictions & corrections

Ufc For Speed

Uses typing-speed information from Gboard’s User Feature Cache (UFC), which retains learned typing characteristics. This is not a general keyboard speed boost.

enable_ufc_for_speed
Find in full AtlasSuggest correction ↗

Interpretation and limitations

This flag is classified under Predictions & corrections with Optional priority and an estimated impact of Usually low.

Evidence level: Interpreted. This interpretation is based on the identifier and surrounding context; exact effects are not independently confirmed.

Research note: Read-only examination of GboardWu 18.5.4 APK found com/google/android/libraries/inputmethod/userfeaturecache/guarder/UfcGuarder, UfcMetricsProcessorModule, UfcUtils, and enable_ufc_for_speed / enable_ufc_for_offset / enable_export_ufc. 'UFC' expansion is supported by the code namespace; exact flag behavior is inferred and not runtime verified.

Research references

  • Google Research — personalized touch offsets and typing speed (background, not flag documentation)

Gboard AI Writing Tools Flags: Rewrite, Style and Model Gates

Explore Gboard's writing tools controls and distinguish a visible rewrite button from actual on-device or service-backed generation.

What you should know

Writing Tools may involve multiple eligibility checks and model dependencies beyond a single enabled flag.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

What the controls seem to separate

The Atlas includes enable_writing_tools_v2, enable_writing_tools_v2_on_toolbar, enable_writing_tools_suggest_style and enable_writing_tools_my_style. These names point at a product surface, its placement and style selection; they do not prove that a particular generative model is loaded. UI presentation and text generation are distinct functions.

Model gates are another layer

enable_ai_core_llm and other language-model identifiers suggest integrations with on-device or system AI components. But the exact requirements depend on Gboard and Android versions, language, device capability, downloadable assets and remote feature eligibility. Showing a button may be easier than producing a result, and an empty result is not necessarily a bug in the toolbar flag.

Test outputs responsibly

Use disposable text, not confidential messages. Compare neutral and formal rewrites, inspect whether the result preserves meaning and verify the destination text field before inserting it. Record whether an action is unavailable, fails to load or produces a response: those outcomes reveal different layers of a feature.

Frequently asked questions

Can one flag unlock all AI writing tools?

No single flag has been shown to bypass every language, model, device and rollout dependency.

Is a rewritten suggestion guaranteed private?

No. The flag name does not establish the processing location or data-handling policy.
